source.title: Sharp description of local minima in the loss landscape of high-dimensional two-layer ReLU neural networks
source.authors: Jie Huang; Bruno Loureiro; Stefano Sarao Mannelli

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests training outcomes and local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks under gradient-based dynamics, using population squared loss and mean-field ODE simulations rather than CIFAR classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own gradient-flow/ODE outcomes, convergence frequencies, and constrained-optimizer results. Cited results from Safran & Shamir and other prior work are not recorded as rows. The study uses Gaussian inputs and population squared loss, not CIFAR classification tasks or corrupted labels.
record.test_reason: The study independently measures convergence to global and spurious minima in realizable two-layer ReLU teacher–student networks, using population-risk gradient-flow ODEs and width sweeps. These results directly test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's central paraphrase is accurate: equal-width networks have attracting families of spurious minima, and extra width changes their stability and increases global convergence while higher-order traps can persist. The authors additionally establish gradient-flow equivalence for SGD under a vanishing-learning-rate scaling. Constrained-optimizer failures concern altered dynamics and, for overwide fixed-norm models, altered realizability; they do not establish failure of the standard-GD width benefit.
record.recipe_differences: Population-risk squared-loss teacher-student two-layer ReLU networks with Gaussian covariates; mean-field ODE and gradient-flow dynamics, plus constrained optimizer variants. No CIFAR classification benchmark, corrupted labels, or standard SGD/Adam benchmark recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Student/teacher width ratio; unconstrained versus normalized or orthonormalized optimizer; in onGD, tested width 2 versus 17 changes success.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed-norm nGD and orthonormalized onGD exhibit positive final losses, slowdowns, and width-dependent learning failures. At K>M, fixed unit norms and readouts also obstruct zero-loss realization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric constraints imposed throughout optimization can alter realizability and convergence in two-layer teacher–student networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Leaky ReLU exhibits anti-aligned units, whereas the displayed erf solutions lack them under nGD at K=M=12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice changes the structure of stationary solutions under constrained teacher–student dynamics.

record.code_released: not stated; source code for mean-field dynamics and fixed-point solvers will be made publicly available upon publication.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026.
record.problems: Population squared loss on Gaussian teacher-student toy networks does not directly measure classification error on CIFAR benchmarks. Main figures include figure-only trajectories and histograms; several frequency classifications use thresholds selected by visual inspection. The abstract and paper do not report uncertainty intervals for the convergence percentages.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result-bearing condition was omitted; cited Safran & Shamir results and results only used as background were excluded. Figure-only settings are represented without reconstructed numeric values.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training error, corrupted labels, convolutional networks, and SGD/Adam benchmark recipes.
The complete two-extra-neuron sweep over teacher widths 6–20; finite-step standard GD frequencies across input dimensions; systematic comparisons of initialization distributions.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and deep plain or residual networks.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, propagation of signals and gradients, learning speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, sharpness evolution, and divergence.
Batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance, accuracy speed, and Fixup.

missing.what: Table 2 reports GD global convergence of 13.25%, 64.18%, and 77.50% at M=17 and K=17,18,19. These support a width benefit but conflict materially with Table 1's 99.63% at K=19. Record these separately and preserve the unresolved discrepancy. Table 2 also reports 2L-GD frequencies of 13.24%, 67.91%, and 99.48%, requiring a separate condition with trained readouts.

The study's perturbation experiment finds selected equal-width spurious fixed points stable, while their embeddings with extra neurons become unstable. This supplies direct mechanistic evidence for the width benefit. The main caption and Appendix D disagree about relaxation duration and the monitored quantity.

Finite-dimensional initialization checks at d=196,392,784 retain nonzero local-minimum loss families and aligned/anti-aligned structure, with broader peaks at smaller dimensions. Record this robustness result without inferring unreported convergence frequencies or widths.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V2. Persistent spurious minima do not alone limit a claim explicitly allowing sharp reduction rather than elimination. The supplied text contains inconsistent convergence statistics and simulation descriptions; those discrepancies should remain visible.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam from random initialization, and the effect of small models, early stopping, or regularization.

Teacher-student width sweep is reported, but not the claim's six-to-twenty-neuron range as a general paired-width experiment; results use population ReLU teacher-student dynamics and do not compare standard initialization variants.
Depth, plain versus residual shortcuts, batch normalization, and deep networks.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rise and recovery, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, accuracy speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-flow ODE dynamics from 104 independent random initialisations drawn from the standard normal distribution; population risk measured at convergence.
rows.measure: Fraction of initialisations reaching global minimum, k1-family frequencies and final population loss distribution.
rows.value: Table 1 reports k1 = 0: 13.09%; k1 = 1: 27.52%; k1 = 2: 29.05%; k1 = 3: 18.94%; k1 = 4: 7.55%. Figure 2 reports a nonzero, quantised final-loss distribution; text says a significant fraction remains trapped in high-loss families.
rows.note: The result shows frequent spurious minima when teacher and student have equal width. The text separately describes 104 initialisations for Figure 2 and Table 1; percentages are reported as printed. This is a population-risk toy problem, not a benchmark classification task.
rows.check: Frequent trapping supports V2; low global-minimum frequency is not a partial effect. The initialization count is 10^4, not 104. The listed family percentages omit higher-order families.

source_check.problem: The initialization count loses its exponent.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-flow ODE dynamics from random initialisations; population risk measured at convergence.
rows.measure: Fraction reaching global minimum and frequency of converged local-minimum families.
rows.value: Table 1: k1 = 0: 59.29%; k1 = 1: 0.00%; k1 = 2: 2.10%; k1 = 3: 10.83%; k1 = 4: 8.99%. Text says nearly all trajectories converge to zero loss in this condition.
rows.note: One extra student unit sharply raises global-minimum frequency and removes the observed k1 = 1 family, while higher-order families persist. Table percentages shown are the reported subset of k1 categories.
rows.check: Increasing global convergence from 13.09% to 59.29% demonstrates the sharp reduction allowed by V2. The prose description of nearly universal convergence conflicts with Table 1 and should not be repeated as this condition's result. Initialization count is 10^4.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-flow ODE trajectories from random initialisations; population risk followed over training steps.
rows.measure: Population-risk trajectories and attraction to discrete loss plateaux or global minimum.
rows.value: Figure 4 shows figure-only loss trajectories; accompanying text says all regimes exhibit entrapment in discrete high-loss plateaux, with mild overparameterisation progressively destabilising intermediate plateaus and allowing more trajectories to reach the global minimum.
rows.note: Text describes a trend, but the plotted curves do not provide exact convergence percentages for these widths.
rows.check: The text establishes improved escape with extra width, but provides no convergence frequencies establishing the magnitude of reduction. Residual plateaux alone do not contradict V2, which allows reduction without elimination.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for the sharpness of the reduction named by V2. Figure 4 reports improved escape with extra width and persistent high-loss plateaux, without convergence frequencies.
source_check.problem: Persistent trapping does not establish a partial effect when V2 permits sharp reduction without elimination.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Normalized gradient descent (nGD) under a fixed student-weight norm constraint; population risk measured after training.
rows.baseline: Unconstrained GD in Table 3a: global 13.18% at K = M = 17
rows.value: Table 4: local 85.88%, global 14.12%, none 0.00% for K = M = 17.
rows.note: This is a constrained-optimizer comparison; global-minimum classification uses a width-specific threshold ε = 1e-2. It does not test V2's standard unconstrained gradient-descent setting directly.
rows.check: Projected dynamics with fixed weight norms do not measure V2's standard gradient-descent behavior. This single-width optimizer comparison does not establish a width effect.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Normalized gradient descent (nGD) under fixed student-weight norms; population loss measured after training.

conditions.value: not stated for Figure 13; 10,000 seeds in related Appendix G.1 table for K=M+1, not this setting

rows.measure: Final population-loss distribution and best-found loss.
rows.baseline: Unconstrained GD reportedly reaches zero loss in the overparameterized setting
rows.value: Text says the system fails to reach the global minima (Loss ≈ 0); even the best-found minima have Loss ≈ 0.355. Figure 13a shows a multimodal distribution.
rows.note: The paper states an explicit failure of overparameterisation under the norm constraint. This qualifies the width benefit by optimizer constraint.
rows.check: Fixed unit norms and fixed unit readouts prevent excess neurons from disappearing, removing the zero-loss realizability premise of V2. The positive loss is not evidence that extra width fails to avoid spurious minima in V2's setting. Figure 13 uses 20 million steps.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Orthonormalized gradient descent (onGD) with student weights constrained to remain orthonormal; population loss measured after training.
rows.measure: Final population-loss distribution and teacher-feature retrieval.
rows.value: Text says onGD does not achieve meaningful learning; final loss distribution is in [0.18, 0.30], with a peak around 0.22; overlaps remain disordered.
rows.note: Constrained dynamics fail in the width-17 case. The comparison does not directly isolate width from the optimizer constraint.
rows.check: Orthonormality is enforced throughout optimization, rather than used only at initialization. Finite-budget failure under these projected dynamics does not measure convergence to spurious minima under standard GD. Figure 13 uses 20 million steps.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Orthonormalized gradient descent (onGD) under student-weight orthogonality constraint; training loss and final teacher overlap measured.
rows.measure: Training loss after optimization and teacher-feature retrieval.
rows.baseline: onGD at K = M = 17, where text reports high-error behavior
rows.value: Figure 16 text describes training loss converging to near-zero (∼ 10−3) and a clear diagonal teacher-student overlap.
rows.note: The authors state successful learning is possible with few hidden units under onGD, unlike their width-17 condition.
rows.check: This representative constrained-optimizer trajectory at width two does not measure V2's standard GD behavior or its stated width range. It supplies no convergence frequency.
